svg.text: 256 phases × 64 taps, 18-bit signed coeffs, 16-bit alpha lerp, 6-stage single-MAC pipeline
Depth = 2 × TAPS so input-side write during a MAC
never lands in the active 64-tap read window.
(servo starts inside its deadband, no transient)
S2 — BRAM / SAMP READ IN FLIGHT
port A → coeff_a_q | port B → coeff_b_q
addresses presented in S1 → data registered at end of S2
samp_q simultaneously available from ring buffer
round-half-up cancels the signal-correlated bias of `≫16`
single multiplier, time-shared across all 64 taps
first-tap reset avoids extra clear cycle
single accumulator; no contention since taps are 1-cycle apart
PIPELINE QUALIFIERS (one bit per stage, advance every clock)
Per-MAC latency = TAPS + 5 = 69 cycles. New MAC launches every TAPS cycles (= 64).
At any cycle each pipeline stage is owned by ≤ 1 MAC ⇒ multiplier & accumulator never contended.
Wrapper must guarantee `out_strobe` separations ≥ TAPS cycles; closer strobes are dropped.
phase 0..255 stored as written; row 256 = duplicate of phase 0
phase_acc[32] → carry ⇒ one input sample consumed
